title: Average of Two Numbers
description: Read two integers a and b and print their average with exactly one decimal place, using (a + b) / 2. This is a targeted remedial probe for C1-M02 (type-coercion-and-division): an integer division (//) or a forgotten conversion silently drops the fractional half, so the odd-sum boundary cases distinguish float-division reasoning from truncating-division reasoning. Like every EvidencePack, a failure here is observed evidence that can help diagnosis, never a deterministic detection on its own.
constraints: Input is two integers separated by a space.
starter_code:
def average_pair(a, b):
    """Return the average of a and b as a float."""

    raise NotImplementedError


def main():
    import sys
    data = sys.stdin.read().strip().split()
    if not data:
        return
    a = int(data[0])
    b = int(data[1])
    print(f"{average_pair(a, b):.1f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
input_format: Two integers a and b separated by a space.
output_format: A single number: the average of a and b with exactly one decimal place.
